chunks: From him, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman in exchange for a room in his house, and he had partners in that house. He said: 'It is permissible for him and for her, and there is no pre-emption (shuf'ah) for any of the partners against her.'

key_terms.تَزَوَّجَ عَلَى بَيْتٍ: Married in exchange for a room/space
key_terms.شُفْعَة: Right of pre-emption (claiming a property share before selling to an outsider)

ai.seo_question: Do partners in a house have the right of pre-emption against a wife's room in a marriage contract?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on a marriage contract involving a specific room in a house shared by partners, declaring the marriage valid and clarifying that the other partners do not have the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) to claim that specific room for the wife. This ruling highlights the flexibility of marital property arrangements in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the wife's exclusive right to the designated space from the general co-ownership rights of the partners. It underscores the principle that the spouse's right to the marital home takes precedence over the partners' potential claim of pre-emption in this specific context.
